mapName: A Learnable Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.name: Bangladesh - Agricultural Fields & Water
metas.note: • Bodies of water and agricultural fields can be often seen beside the streets of Bangladesh.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bangladesh for more clues.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Gen 3 Cars
metas.note:
- In Generation 3 coverage, these three cars can be seen in Bangladesh:

  • The red mirror with bars, classic white and striped white car.

--- NOTE:

  • The classic white car is the only car that is not unique to Bangladesh.
  • Make sure to not mix up the striped white with the Cambodian car, since they look similar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bangladesh for more clues.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Gen 4 Cars
metas.note:
- In Generation 4 coverage, two Street View cars can be seen in Bangladesh:

  • A black car and a white car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bangladesh for more clues.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Rickshaws
metas.note:
• Rickshaws are frequently found all around Bangladesh, especially the green auto rickshaws.

--- NOTE:

  • They are found in other Asian countries as well.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bangladesh for more clues.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Shitcam
metas.note:
• Bangladesh, as well as a variety of other countries, has received some poor quality coverage, also known as “Shitcam”.
  • The Shitcam car colours are black and white.

--- NOTE:

  • Sometimes the car colour can be fully obstructed by a big circular blur.

--- TIP:

  • Shitcam is only found around Dhaka.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bangladesh for more clues.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• Signposts in Bangladesh often have black-and-white stripes.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Asia, these posts are also found in Sri Lanka, Bhutan, India and Malaysia.
  • Make sure to check other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bangladesh for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - Architecture
metas.note:
• The traditional Bhutanese architecture is very distinct.
  • Most of the houses have tin roofs and wooden painted frames, which give them a unique look.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bhutan for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - Car
metas.note:
• Coverage in Bhutan was taken by a grey Google car without an antenna.

--- NOTE:

  • Bhutan is the only left hand driving country which has a grey Google car.
  • Make sure to not mix it up with a white Google car, since they can look similar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bhutan for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - Landscape
metas.note:
• Bhutan is a mountainous country and most of the coverage is located on its main mountain roads.

--- NOTE:

  • In the south are flat areas where you cannot see any mountains.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bhutan for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - License Plates
metas.note:
• Licence plates in Bhutan are almost always red and can easily be seen on vehicles.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Asia, Bhutan is the only country that uses full red licence plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bhutan for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - Painted Poles
metas.note:
• Thin metal poles are occasionally found in Bhutan.
  • They are often painted black at the bottom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bhutan for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - Stone Blocks
metas.note:
• Bhutan commonly uses these stone blocks as safety barriers on winding rural roads.
  • These blocks are very common and often one of the best ways to recognize rural Bhutan rounds.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bhutan for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Bollards
metas.note:
Cambodia has a variety of different bollards. The most common ones are:

  • A stone bollard with red-and-white stripes.
  • A stone bollard with a red top and a white base, usually with a reflector in the red part.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Gen 3 Cars
metas.note:
--- GENERATION 3 CARS:

  • A car with a short, stubby antenna.
  • The antenna has three ridges.

➖➖➖➖➖

  • A white car with stripes and no antenna.
  • There is a white stripe on the left, and a yellow stripe on the right.

--- NOTE:

  • This specific striped white car is unique to Cambodia.
  • Make sure not to mix it up with the Bangladeshi striped car, which looks slightly different.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Houses On Stilts
metas.note:
• Wooden houses on stilts are common.
  • Walls are often made of vertical planks.
  • Many homes have double or triple roofs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Poles
metas.note:
Two types of poles are common:

  • Concrete ladder poles (so named because the indents and ridges resemble a ladder).
  • Round concrete poles with small holes.
  • Rarely, you might see simple wooden poles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Roads have dashed or solid yellow middle road lines.
  • Outer road lines are somewhat rare, but when present, they are solid white.

--- NOTE:

  • Thailand uses similar road lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Shitcam
metas.note:
• Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Cambodia.
  • This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”).
  • It has a wide circular car blur and often somewhat brownish colours.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Asia, India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka also have shitcam coverage.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Hong Kong - Air Conditioners
metas.note: • Because of the subtropical climate, air conditioners attached to the walls of apartments are very common in Hong Kong.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hong Kong - Road Signs
metas.note: • Road signs are white and rectangular, with a thick black outline and bilingual text.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hong Kong - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Hong Kong usually uses white centre lines and white or yellow outer lines.
  • These lines can be single, double or dashed.
  • Yellow outer lines are most commonly found on small roads to indicate no-stopping.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hong Kong - Tall Buildings
metas.note:
• One very striking aspect of Hong Kong architecture are the many extremely tall apartment buildings found throughout the city.

--- NOTE:

  • Apartment buildings in Singapore and Taiwan tend to be not nearly as tall as those in Hong Kong.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hong Kong - Taxis
metas.note:
Hong Kong taxis come in two variants:

  • Sedans or station wagons, with the sedans most commonly seen.
  • They can be easily identified by their silver roofs, green stickers on the front and rear bumper, and the taxi sign on the roof.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hong Kong - Vibes
metas.note:
• Hong Kong is a densely populated city with millions of inhabitants.
  • In urban areas, modern skyscrapers are common, with busy streets filled with vehicles and pedestrians.
  • In many cases, this vibe alone should be sufficient to identify urban Hong Kong locations.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: India - License Plates
metas.note:
• Indian licence plates are typically fairly long, with the most common design being white.
  • Commercial vehicles typically use yellow plates, while electric vehicles use green.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Shitcam
metas.note:
• The vast majority of the coverage in India was taken with what’s commonly referred to as “shitcam”.
  • It's a low-quality camera that can typically be recognised by the brownish colours and often, but not always, by a large circular blur covering the Street View car.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Asia, shitcam coverage is also common in Cambodia and can rarely be seen in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• India typically has black and white striped signposts.

--- NOTE:

  • Bangladesh and Sri Lanka also have black and white signposts.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Bollards
metas.note:
• Indonesia commonly uses these black-and-white square or circular bollards, as well as these yellow-and-black ones, which can also have a red reflector.
  • Other designs can also be found.

--- NOTE:

  • UK-style bollards are mostly found in Kalimantan.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - License Plates
metas.note:
• Indonesian licence plates are black with white letters.
  • The letters usually appear as three white sections through the blur.
  • Plates in newer coverage can be white too.

--- NOTE:

  • Malaysian licence plates are also black, but generally have two white sections.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Motorcycle Front Plates
metas.note: • Motorcycles in Indonesia have front licence plates, as opposed to other south-east Asian countries which do not.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Poles
metas.note:
• Poles in Indonesia are typically round and made out of either steel or concrete.
  • Many of the steel poles are painted black, and also feature the Indonesian flag colours on them.
  • The pole tops are usually either even or uneven, depending on the region.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Indonesia uses white or yellow centre lines.
  • Outer lines will always be white.
  • The centre lines will be solid or dashed.

--- NOTE:

  • In Generation 3 coverage, yellow centre lines are more rare, as Indonesia only recently started using this colour for its road lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Chevrons
metas.note: • Chevrons are white on black.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Curbs
metas.note:
• You will very often see striped kerbs.
  • Red and white and fairly commonly black and white.
  • Red and yellow and blue and white are also rarely found.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Gen 3 Black Car
metas.note:
• Most Generation 3 coverage was taken by a black Street View car with a long antenna.
  • You may also see the black car without an antenna and a silver car with a short antenna.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Kilometre Markers
metas.note: • Kilometre markers are white with a thick border, which can either be red, green or blue.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - License Plates
metas.note:
• Israeli licence plates are yellow with a blue strip on the left.

--- NOTE:

  • While this design is specific for Israel, it is also very common on the West Bank.
  • Jordan and the UAE use white licence plates.
  • Tunisia uses black plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Painted Poles
metas.note: • Utility poles commonly feature these painted black and white striped bottoms.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Roadlines
metas.note: • Most roads feature yellow outer lines with white centre lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Stop Sign
metas.note: • Rather than having a word meaning ‘stop’ written on them, stop signs have a hand painted on them.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture
metas.note:
• Japanese architecture has many distinct and expressive styles, with many unique buildings.
  • These can range from traditional country houses, regional designs, modern large cities, coastal reinforced buildings, and anything in between.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Bollards
metas.note:
• Japan usually uses simple white bollards with circular reflector(s) on the top.
  • However, sometimes these bollards are black, or have other extensions.
  • They can also have the city or prefecture written on it in kanji.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - License Plates
metas.note:
• Japan uses a standard short white licence plate with green text.
  • You will often see a different short yellow version with black text issued to “light automobiles”, otherwise known as Kei Cars.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Lowcam
metas.note:
Due to privacy reasons, the camera is intentionally set lower to the ground.

This is known as low-cam.

You can identify it by:

  • Looking downwards.
  • The blur will be noticeably larger.
  • The road will look wider, and objects will be viewed from a lower perspective.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Poles
metas.note:
Japan mostly uses these round concrete poles, which have these screw-like extensions.

Other information can often be found on or attached to the pole including:

  • Electrical plates.
  • Guy-wires.
  • Pole reflectors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Retaining Walls
metas.note: • Retaining walls can be an excellent clue for Japan in rural areas with little to no information.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Jordan - Architecture
metas.note:
• Most buildings in Jordan are made of bright sandstone bricks and have flat roofs.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar sandstone bricks are also common in Jerusalem.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/jordan for more clues.

metas.name: Jordan - Black Car
metas.note:
• Coverage in Jordan was taken by a black Google car, without a red brake light.

--- NOTE:

  • Jordan is the only Middle Eastern country where a black Google car without an antenna or a red brake light can be found.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/jordan for more clues.

metas.name: Jordan - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Jordanian chevrons are white with red arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • You can use chevrons to distinguish between Jordan and Israel:
  • The Israeli chevrons are black with white arrows.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/jordan for more clues.

metas.name: Jordan - License Plates
metas.note:
• Jordanian licence plates are white and can be long or short.
  • Commercial transport vehicles, such as taxis, have a distinctive green strip on the left.

--- NOTE:

  • In the Middle East, the green strip is only found in Jordan.
  • The UAE also uses long white plates.
  • Israel however only uses yellow licence plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/jordan for more clues.

metas.name: Jordan - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Roads in Jordan typically feature yellow outside and white middle lines.

--- NOTE:

  • Other Middle Eastern countries such as the UAE and Israel can also have these road lines.
  • Make sure to check other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/jordan for more clues.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Bollards
metas.note:
• Kazakhstan uses a variety of post-Soviet style bollards, as well as ones that resemble Turkish bollards.
  • Notably, the bollards seemingly consisting of two thin bollards attached at a 90° angle are unique to Kazakhstan.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Car
metas.note: • All of the coverage in Kazakhstan was taken with a white pickup truck, which can either be fully visible or mostly blurred.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Gas Pipes
metas.note: • Gas pipes are extremely common in Kazakh cities.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Landscape
metas.note:
• Kazakhstan is a big and diverse country, which features a plethora of distinct landscapes like deserts, grassy steppes, mountain passes, and birch forests.
  • Most strikingly, most of the rural coverage in Kazakhstan is in a very empty, open and mostly flat landscape.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Pedestrian Crossing
metas.note:
• Like Russia, Kazakhstan uses yellow and white stripes on their pedestrian crossings.
  • However, unlike Russia the stripes often have white dashes on either side.
  • Sometimes, you can find the dashes without the stripes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Russian Infrastructure
metas.note: • A lot of Kazakh infrastructure, from pedestrian signs, poles, houses, to bollards, is very similar to what you see in Russia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Bollards
metas.note: • Kyrgyzstan uses these simple white bollards with a diagonal black stripe near the top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Car
metas.note:
• Kyrgyzstan can be recognised from the silver car and four bars that are visible.
  • All coverage is Generation 3.

--- NOTE:

  • No other country with a similar landscape has a similar Street View car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Landscape
metas.note: • All of Kyrgyzstan was covered during the winter months, so many of the trees will lack leaves, the landscape will be quite drab, and you can see snow in many parts of Kyrgyzstan.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - License Plates
metas.note:
• Licence plates in Kyrgyzstan have a red strip on them.

--- NOTE:

  • Licence plates with red strips can sometimes be seen in Albania and very rarely in the UAE.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan for more clues.

metas.name: Laos - License Plates
metas.note:
• Laotian licence plates are short and yellow.
  • This distinguishes them from nearby Thailand and Cambodia, who both use white plates on non-commercial vehicles.
  • Laotian commercial plates are white, and government plates are blue.

--- NOTE:

  • Thailand uses yellow plates for commercial vehicles, such as taxis.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/laos for more clues.

metas.name: Laos - Unique Car
metas.note:
• In all cities except for the capital, Vientiane, this Google car will be visible.
  • It is silver-coloured, with a roof rack with two metal bars and black side mirrors.

--- NOTE:

  • A similar car can be found in Guatemala, so be sure to look at the other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/laos for more clues.

metas.name: Macau - Gen 2
metas.note:
• Coverage in Macau is limited to Generation 2.
  • Generation 2 can be recognized by the lower camera quality and circular blur above and below the camera.
  • The coverage in Macau specifically is some of the oldest Generation 2 available, meaning that the colours look even more washed out and overexposed than usual.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Macau - License Plates
metas.note:
• Macau uses black licence plates with white text.
  • Licence plates can either be long or square.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Bollards
metas.note:
• Malaysian bollards will often have the colours black, white, grey and red.

--- NOTE:

  • There can be multiple varieties of these bollards, but the layout is mostly the same.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Directional Signs
metas.note:
• This is a typical Malaysian directional sign.
  • Hexagonal yellow highway shields are unique to Malaysia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - License Plates
metas.note:
• Malaysian licence plates are black and generally have two white sections.
  • These are visible even when blurred.

--- NOTE:

  • Indonesian licence plates are also black, but they will have three white sections.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Pole Sticker
metas.note:
• Electricity poles in Malaysia often have black or white stickers on them.
  • Sometimes you will also find red-and-white or red-and-blue stripes below the black sticker.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Malaysia frequently uses double white centre lines on its two-lane roads.
  • It is the only Southeast Asian country to do so.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Stop Sign
metas.note: • BERHENTI stop signs and BERI LALUAN yield signs are both unique to Malaysia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• Signposts in Malaysia almost always have black-and-white stripes.

--- NOTE:

  • Within South-East Asia, these posts are also found in Sri Lanka, Bhutan and Bangladesh.
  • Make sure to check other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Yellow Bars
metas.note:
• These thick yellow bars are also almost exclusive to Malaysia.

--- NOTE:

  • You can very rarely see similar patterns in Hong Kong and the United Kingdom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Bollards
metas.note: • Mongolia uniquely features white bowling-pin shaped bollards with two red stripes around the top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Cars
metas.note:
• Mongolia very often has a visible Street View car as all of Mongolian coverage was driven with a large pickup truck.
  • The truck can have several features such as a tent on top, red side-view mirrors, a snorkel, and roof-racks.
  • All of these can be of help in identifying Mongolia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Landscape
metas.note:
• Mongolia can typically be identified by the steppe biomes found across the country.
  • While some forested areas are found in Mongolia, most of the country features empty grasslands or deserts with a characteristic lack of trees.

--- NOTE:

  • It is not uncommon to find rugged, rocky or rolling hills as well as rivers and lakes across Mongolia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Round Yurts
metas.note: • White, round yurts are the traditional dwelling of nomadic families in Mongolia, and are often seen all around the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Car
metas.note: • All the coverage in Oman was taken with a white pickup truck, meaning you will either see most of the car or a large front blur.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Chevrons
metas.note: • Oman uses black-and-yellow chevrons that have an unusually large number of arrows.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Curbs
metas.note:
• Black-and-yellow curbs are common in Oman.

--- NOTE:

  • The UAE also commonly uses similar curbs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Garbage Bins
metas.note:
• The vast majority of garbage bins in Oman are either black and made of plastic or metallic and grey, with a three-leaf logo and the text ‘be’ah’ below it.

--- NOTE:

  • Garbage bins in the UAE will occasionally have the text “bee’ah”, with two E’s.
  • The bins are often more colourful too.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - High Voltage Pylons
metas.note:
• High voltage pylons painted with a red and white pattern are common in Oman.

--- NOTE:

  • Within the Middle East, red and white painted pylons can also less commonly be found in Qatar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Landscape
metas.note:
• Most of Oman features a desert landscape with little vegetation.
  • While the middle and southern half is mostly flat, the north coast features dry mountains similar to those found in the UAE.
  • The southern coast also has mountains, though less dry.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - License Plates
metas.note: • Licence plates on private vehicles are generally yellow, while commercial vehicles have red plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Roads in Oman use yellow outer and white middle lines.

--- NOTE:

  • This is also common in the UAE, Israel, Jordan, as well as occasionally found in Qatar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• Many signposts in Oman have black-and-white stripes.

--- NOTE:

  • Within the Middle East, striped signposts are only found in Oman and the UAE.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Chevrons
metas.note: • Chevrons are typically red on white.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Concrete Roads
metas.note:
• Concrete roads are extremely common in the Philippines.

--- NOTE:

  • Thailand also has a lot of concrete roads.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Gen 3 Black Roof
metas.note:
• In Generation 3 you can come across a white Street View car with the black roof clearly visible.
  • You may also come across a silvery grey car, which is also found in Bhutan.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Poles
metas.note:
• Octagonal metal poles are quite common in the Philippines.

--- NOTE:

  • They can sometimes be found in Bangladesh and some parts of Malaysia as well.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Middle road lines in the Philippines can be either yellow or white.
  • In particular, you will often see combined yellow and white middle lines, which is not common in any other East Asian country.
  • Yellow road lines commonly have a distinct orange tint.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Single Insulator
metas.note: • You will often see a single insulator at the top of a vertical bar which is attached to the side of a utility pole.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Tuk-Tuks
metas.note: • Tuk-tuks, also referred to as tricycles, are extremely common in the Philippines, in many areas they are more common than typical cars.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - Car
metas.note:
• The Google car will usually be blurred, with only the antenna on the left and a sliver of the car visible.
  • Sometimes the entire white pickup truck can be visible.
  • Rusty clips can be seen on the crossbar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - Chevrons
metas.note: • Qatar uses white on red and white on blue chevrons.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - Landscape
metas.note:
• Qatar's landscape is predominantly desert, with arid, and mostly flat expanses of sand as far as the eye can see.
  • You will often not see a lot of trees or other greenery.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - License Plates
metas.note:
• Regular cars in Qatar have long, white licence plates with a maroon strip on the left.
  • Trucks have square, black licence plates and police plates are blue.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - Pedestrian Sign
metas.note: • Qatari crossing signs feature a man in a thobe.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - Poles
metas.note:
• Qatar uses round poles with 3 insulators on the pole top, with the middle one being slightly higher.
  • The crossbar also has 2 diagonal bars connecting it to the pole.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Qatar typically uses solid outer white lines with either white or yellow in the middle.
  • More rarely, you can also find outer yellow lines too.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Singapore - Buses
metas.note:
• Singaporean buses are mostly lime-green, making them easily recognisable.
  • Other designs can also be found, for example the white-and-purple SBS Transit variants.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/singapore for more clues.

metas.name: Singapore - Road Signs
metas.note:
• Road signs in Singapore are unique in that they are always set on a square white background.

--- NOTE:

  • Road signs in almost all other countries will not have this square background.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/singapore for more clues.

metas.name: Singapore - Street Signs
metas.note:
• All street name signs in Singapore follow this unique format.
  • They are green, with rounded edges and a distinct white font.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/singapore for more clues.

metas.name: Singapore - Vibes
metas.note:
• Singapore is a highly developed city-state, characterised by an overall cleanliness and orderliness.
  • Main roads are often divided, and commonly feature black-and-white curbs and double yellow outside lines.
  • You will often see tall apartment blocks nearby.

--- NOTE:

  • In many cases, this “general look” is all you need to easily identify Singapore.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/singapore for more clues.

metas.name: Singapore - Warnings On Roads
metas.note: • Warnings are often written on the road in large letters, such as the famous “HUMP AHEAD”.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/singapore for more clues.

metas.name: South Korea - Autumn & Winter
metas.note:
• A considerable amount of the coverage was made during autumn and winter.
  • Note that more pleasant-looking spring and summer coverage is also not uncommon.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-korea for more clues.

metas.name: South Korea - Cars
metas.note:
• Almost all road coverage in South Korea is made with a Generation 3 camera.
  • In most, but not all, of the coverage, the back of the Google car is visible.

You can see three colours:

  • Black, white and silver.
  • The car never has an antenna.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-korea for more clues.

metas.name: South Korea - Pole Sticker
metas.note:
• Utility poles almost always have these pole markings near the bottom, consisting of black and yellow diagonal stripes.

These markings look similar to the ones found in Taiwan. There are however two main differences:

  • In South Korea, the stripes do not reach all the way to the bottom, whereas in Taiwan they do.
  • In South Korea, the stripes are more yellow. In Taiwan, they have more of an orange tint.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-korea for more clues.

metas.name: South Korea - Spike Pole
metas.note: • Most poles have a tapered “spike” on top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-korea for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Bollards
metas.note:
• These short, wide stone bollards are unique to Sri Lanka.
  • They have a tapered shape, with a black base and a white top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Gen 3 French Car
metas.note:
In most Generation 3 coverage, you will be able to see the front of the Google car partially through the blur:

  • It is visible as blue-white-red patches, reminiscent of the French flag.
  • The red patch is usually most visually distinct.

--- NOTE:

  • This car is unique to Sri Lanka.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Gen 4 Lowcam
metas.note:
• All Generation 4 coverage is low-cam.

This can be recognized in two ways:

  • The car blur is significantly bigger.
  • Roads look wider and objects around you are seen from a lower angle.

--- NOTE:

  • Sri Lanka’s Generation 3 coverage is made with a normal height camera!
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - License Plates
metas.note: • Vehicles in Sri Lanka have long white front plates and short yellow rear plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Mushroom Insulator
metas.note: • Throughout Sri Lanka, you will very commonly see insulators that look like mushrooms.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Rural roads often have outside lines, but no middle lines.
  • In the absence of other clues, this can sometimes be a way to decide a tough 50-50.

--- NOTE:

  • Most small roads lack road lines entirely.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Shitcam
metas.note:
• Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Sri Lanka.
  • This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”).
  • It has a wide circular car blur and often somewhat brownish colours.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Asia, India and Cambodia also have shitcam coverage.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• Sri Lanka commonly uses black and white striped signposts.

--- NOTE:

  • Within South and Southeast Asia, such signposts are also found in Bangladesh, India and Malaysia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Taiwan - Gen 3 Black Car
metas.note: • In Generation 3 coverage, you can find this black car with a long antenna and a red brake light in the middle, similar to the one you can see in Russia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/taiwan for more clues.

metas.name: Taiwan - Pole Sticker
metas.note:
• Poles almost always feature these black and yellow diagonal-striped markings that run all the way to the bottom.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar markings can be seen in South Korea.
  • However, the markings are much shorter and do not run all the way to the bottom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/taiwan for more clues.

metas.name: Taiwan - Roadlines
metas.note:
--- YELLOW LINES:

  • Roads in Taiwan generally feature double yellow middle lines with single white outer lines.

--- WHITE LINES:

  • Roads with outside white road lines and no middle lines at all are common.
  • In the absence of better clues, this type of road line can be a very good way to identify Taiwan.

--- RED LINES:

  • Red outer lines that indicate no parking are common in Taiwan, especially in cities.
  • This is essentially unique to the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/taiwan for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Bollards
metas.note:
• The Thai bollard is square shaped with a pointed top, and has black-and-white stripes.

--- NOTE:

  • In Southeast Asia, these bollards are also found in Cambodia, Laos and Indonesia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Bulky Signposts
metas.note:
• Signposts in Thailand are square and bulky in shape, usually white, and often have the bottom painted black.

--- NOTE:

  • In Southeast Asia, this design is unique to Thailand.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Concrete Roads
metas.note:
• Concrete roads are common in Thailand.
  • They often have a large square shaped pattern.

--- NOTE:

  • In Southeast Asia, these can also be found commonly in the Philippines, and less commonly in Indonesia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Lamp Posts
metas.note: • Thailand has very distinct long, thin lamp posts that hang over the side of the road.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Painted Poles
metas.note: • Street light poles have red-and-black or black-and-white stripes on the bottom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Pole
metas.note:
• Thai poles are square and have small holes running vertically up the pole.

--- NOTE:

  • You will see similar poles in Sri Lanka, Cambodia and Laos.
  • Make sure to look for other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Thailand has yellow middle lines.
  • These middle lines are either solid or dashed lines.

--- NOTE:

  • Malaysia only has white middle lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Apartment Blocks
metas.note: • Tall and somewhat square apartment blocks are very common in Turkey.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Bollards
metas.note:
• Turkish bollards have a simple design: rectangular, plain white, and with a red reflector on the front.
  • They are thin when seen from the side.

--- NOTE:

  • Romania has similar bollards.
  • However, bollards are relatively rare in Romania.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Turkish chevrons are typically red on white.
  • Beware that there are some other regional variants.
  • Usually, the tip of the arrow does not touch the edge of the chevron.
  • Some chevrons have a neon yellow border.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Gen 3 No Antenna
metas.note: • In the Generation 3 coverage, the Google car never has an antenna.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Gen 4 Truck
metas.note:
• A grey pickup truck can be found in some Generation 4 coverage.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar pickup trucks can also be found in Senegal and Kenya.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Gen 4 White Car
metas.note:
• The Generation 4 coverage in Turkey typically features a white Google car.
  • Usually, only a tiny sliver of the back of the car is visible.
  • The car can have a short antenna, or no antenna at all.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Roadlines
metas.note:
• The colour of Turkish road lines is somewhat inconsistent.
  • Most roads simply have white road lines.
  • However, it is not uncommon to see yellow road lines.
  • These roads can have fully yellow lines, or a combination of yellow and white lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Salt & Pepper Roads
metas.note: • Many roads have pavement with a grainy “salt and pepper” texture.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Stop Sign
metas.note:
• Stop signs have the word “DUR” written on them.
  • This is unique to Turkey.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Curbs
metas.note:
• Similarly, almost all curbs are striped.
  • They can be either black-and-white, or black-and-yellow.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Gen 3 Car
metas.note:
• In almost all Generation 3 coverage, a white car with visible black roof racks was used.

--- NOTE:

  • The UAE is the only Middle Eastern country where a white Google car can be found.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Gen 4 Black Car
metas.note:
• You can also find regular Generation 4 coverage taken with a black car.
  • The brake light is commonly visible.

--- NOTE:

  • A similar Generation 4 black car can be found in Israel.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Gen 4 Truck
metas.note:
• In Generation 4 coverage, a white pickup truck with a trekker camera was used for much of the coverage.
  • In a lot of the coverage, the truck is completely blurred out.

--- NOTE:

  • A similar truck can be found in Qatar and Oman.
  • In the UAE the antenna at the front of the cabin is on the middle of the car, while in Qatar it is on the left.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Landscape
metas.note: • The UAE typically features a flat desert landscape.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Poles
metas.note:
• Electricity poles in the UAE are mostly made of dark brown wood.
  • The pole tops consist of three insulators, symmetrically attached to a horizontal metal bar.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar poletops can be found in Oman.
  • Jordanian poletops may look similar, but they are usually made of grey concrete, and the insulators are more spaced out.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Reddish Sidewalks
metas.note:
• Houses in residential areas are typically made of light-coloured stone.
  • Reddish stones are often used for sidewalks.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Outer roadlines are yellow, middle lines either white or yellow.

--- NOTE:

  • Other Middle Eastern countries, like Jordan, Israel and Oman, also use these lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Unpaved Roads
metas.note: • Although the UAE is a wealthy country, it is not uncommon for residential roads to be unpaved.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.
